title: Priority prefetch and burst-control for embeddings ingress
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Large tenants and bursty workloads intermittently saturate the embeddings ingress queue, causing high p99 latency and tail retries. Current autoscalers react too slowly for short spikes and lack a mechanism to preferentially serve high-value requests (paid customers, low-latency SLAs). Goal: Implement a lightweight priority-prefetch + burst-control mechanism at the embeddings ingress that reduces tail latency for prioritized traffic, smooths transient surges without aggressive global upsizing, and interfaces with the autoscaler to pre-warm capacity when predictive load signals indicate an incoming sustained uplift. Non-goals: Replace global provisioning policies or redesign the core autoscaler; we will not change model-serving kernels in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: High-priority requests (labelled by tenant tier) see >=40% reduction in p99 latency during bursts compared to baseline (measured on canary pool)
Total dropped requests remain <=0.5% under a 5x synthetic burst above baseline for 2 minutes
Autoscaler receives pre-warm hints and increases warm-pool capacity within configured SLA (default 45s) for predicted sustained increases
Feature can be toggled per-tenant via runtime config flag and has an off-by-default rollout
Comprehensive dashboards and alerts created: ingress-qps, p50/p95/p99 per-priority, prefetch-success-rate, prewarm-latency
plan: 1) Design priority buckets and prefetch policy (this doc). 2) Implement ingress adapter that tags requests with priority and estimated cost. 3) Add burst-controller that enforces token-bucket based admission per-priority and coordinates short-term prefetch into warm pools. 4) Emit hints to autoscaler: predicted-qps(window=60s), jitter score, prewarm-request. 5) End-to-end tests with synthetic traffic, canary rollout on 10% of embeddings capacity, monitor metrics, iterate. 6) Gradual ramp to 100% with rollback gates.
implementation_notes: - Priority assignment is driven by tenant metadata available at request time (tier, SLA flags). - Use a lightweight in-proc token-bucket to avoid RPC hotspots; sync periodically with distributed lease for accurate global quotas. - Prefetch will proactively allocate ephemeral warm slots by requesting short-lived capacity from the provisioner API labeled 'prefetch:ephemeral'. - To avoid over-provisioning, prefetch has a configurable decay and a hard cap per-tenant. - All telemetry instruments correlation IDs so that we can trace end-to-end lifecycle from ingress to model-serving.
tests: Unit tests for token-bucket and priority mapping logic
Integration tests simulating mixed-tenancy bursts with k6 and local dev cluster
Load test: 2-minute 5x burst with weighted tenants; measure p99 and dropped requests
Chaos test: sudden warm-pool shrink during spike to test graceful degradation and fallback policies
rollout_strategy: Feature flagged gate per-tenant. Start with internal tenants and selected paying customers. Canary on 10% of embeddings capacity for 48h with automated metric checks. If p99 increases >5% for non-priority traffic or drop_rate >0.5%, roll back immediately. Post-canary 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 24h observation windows.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Prefetch may trigger unnecessary autoscaler upsizes. Mitigation: implement conservative prewarm hints and a ceiling per-tenant; autoscaler will ignore ephemeral prefetch if sustained growth not observed.
Risk: Priority plumbing could be abused by tenant sprawl. Mitigation: require admin approval and attach billing tags; enforce rate caps for newly promoted tenants.
Risk: Inaccurate predictive signals leading to oscillation. Mitigation: add smoothing window and hysteresis; instrument and put observability-led tripwires.
Risk: Single-node token-bucket desync in multi-region. Mitigation: use lease refresh and fallback to local enforcement with best-effort sync; measure divergence metrics.
Risk: Increased operational complexity. Mitigation: keep the initial implementation small and reversible; document runbook and add synthetic monitors for regression detection.
